ld.name: Kamares Boutique Hotel in Ioannina
ld.description: Only a handful of historic buildings survived the fire that swept through the Greek castle town of Ioannina in 1820. One of these, a handsome stone mansion near the castle walls, is now home to Kamares Boutique Hotel. Much of its old-world grandeur remains — heavy wooden doors, brick archways, ornate fireplaces, sumptuous antiques, and original tile flooring. Rooms exude period charm, too, with exposed stone or brick walls, decorative bedframes, and vaulting wood-beamed ceilings.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Stoes Boutique Hotel in Ioannina
ld.description: Around the corner from Ioannina Castle, an old stone archway leads into the elegant Stoes Boutique Hotel. This mansion dates back to the late 19th century, and much of its old-world character has been preserved, but the hotel’s aesthetic is clean and contemporary — high ceilings, whitewashed walls, gleaming black-and-white tiled floors, a well-placed chandelier.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Domes White Coast Milos in Milos
ld.description: If Greek-island luxury hospitality sometimes feels formulaic, it’s because the formula is just about perfect: luxe accommodations, ocean views, Mediterranean flavors, and an atmosphere that’s laid all the way back. The best hotels in the genre excel because of the details, and in the case of Domes White Coast Milos it might be the modernist simplicity of the design that sets it apart, above all else; it looks fantastic, and it’s got everything else taken care of, from the private pools that come with each unit to the open-air restaurant on the terrace overlooking the ever-impressive Aegean seascape.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Noma Milos in Milos
ld.description: Perched high over the Aegean on a remote stretch of the island’s southern coastline, Noma Milos is a sophisticated and sustainably built boutique hotel with sweeping water views. Rooms and suites are modern and high-ceilinged, outfitted in calming earth tones, with private sea-facing patios and minimalist furnishings in wood, stone, and clay. It’s a place designed for romantic getaways — each room has a single king-sized bed, and no children are allowed — and apart from a massage or a wine tasting, there's nothing to do except lounge around and enjoy the idyllic surroundings. When temptation strikes to dip in the crystalline water in the distance, the nearest beach is just a few minutes’ drive down the hill.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Bold Type Hotel in Patras
ld.description: In Patras, on the northwest coast of the Peloponnese, the perfectly preserved structure of a 19th-century neoclassical residence serves as the backdrop for audaciously minimalist contemporary interiors by architect Empi Spathi. The Bold Type is as luxurious as its design is bold, from its swanky rooms and suites with their Bauhaus and Danish modernist influences to its restaurant, in a tranquil courtyard behind the old house, serving upscale Mediterranean fare in a setting that feels like something straight out of a mid-century cinematic romance.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Elix by Mar-Bella Collection in Perdika
ld.description: The Mar-Bella Collection is a group of stylish and luxurious resorts located mainly in Corfu. Elix rivals any island hotel in terms of visual appeal, yet it stands on the mainland, overlooking the idyllic Karavostasi Beach and the island of Corfu in the distance.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Argini Syros in Syros
ld.description: This island’s gorgeous beaches and rich cultural history form the backdrop for Argini Syros, a 19th-century private residence that’s been transformed into a magnificent 11-room luxury boutique hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Aristide Hotel in Syros
ld.description: Syros’s status as one of the less-traveled Cycladic islands doesn’t preclude it from being home to one of the most attractive hotels in the region. A Neoclassical and Art Deco mansion in the old center of Hermoupolis is now the Aristide Hotel, a passion project for author, economist, and climate activist Oana Aristide. It’s as green as can be in the sustainable sense, and remarkably colorful in the literal sense; the interiors are eclectic, luxurious, and full of carefully selected contemporary artworks. The hotel’s kitchen serves a menu that draws heavily on local and organic ingredients, some grown on-site; the rooftop bar is a little slice of heaven.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Montanema Handmade Village in Thessaly
ld.description: In 1999, a hiker named Christos Athanasiadis came across a small wooden hut in the fog of the Anthochori gorge, among fir, walnut and cedar trees, 4.5 kilometers from Lake Plastira, and liked it enough to build a village around it. Stone by stone, Montanema grew into a cluster of cottages, mansions and villas where exposed timber, open fireplaces and wood-burning stoves define the atmosphere. Three wood-fired ovens and a kitchen garden supply the restaurant; the cellar is stocked with wines from small Greek producers. Deeply handmade, in every sense.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Dexamenes Seaside Hotel in Amaliada
ld.description: Once a winery, this beachside plot in the western Peloponnese has found its true calling, its weathered century-old concrete forms converted into the stunning, industrial-chic Dexamenes Seaside Hotel. Here owner Nikos Karaflos and architects K-Studio have achieved maximal effect with light-handed interventions, removing the winemaking machinery and converting the concrete storage tanks one-to-one into hotel rooms.
ld.petsAllowed: Our hotel is pet friendly but we can accommodate only dogs.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Anthology of Athens in Athens
ld.description: Ideally located for lovers of ancient monuments, Anthology of Athens stands between the Acropolis and what remains of the Temple of Olympian Zeus; many rooms, in fact, look directly out over the columns and toppled stones of the latter site. It takes some confident contemporary architecture to stand confidently in such company, but this five-story structure is up to the task.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: ERGON House Athens in Athens
ld.description: Ergon House is first and foremost a multi-pronged food market, featuring a butcher, a fishmonger, a baker, a grocer, and a restaurant, all under the same Ergon Foods banner that’s been exporting upmarket Greek flavors all across Europe for a decade. It just so happens that above this “modern-day Agora” is a 38-room boutique hotel — and the hotel, it turns out, is no afterthought, but a fully realized holistic hospitality experience, one that takes service and comfort as seriously as it takes its cuisine.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Four Seasons Astir Palace Hotel Athens

ld.name: Four Seasons Astir Palace Hotel Athens in Athens
ld.description: On the Athens Riviera, 30 miles from the city center, the Sixties-era Astir Palace has been brought squarely into the 21st century as a part of the ever-luxe Four Seasons family. Its distinctive terraced construction means the views from the spacious balconies are still as abundant as ever; the interiors are sedate compared to the Sixties but quite stylish, and they’re faultlessly luxurious. Creature comforts are plentiful — the pools, the spa, the sea-facing cabanas — and among its several bars and restaurants the flagship, Pelagos, is the proud recipient of a MICHELIN Star.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

address.streetAddress: 1 Vasileos Georgiou A Str., Syntagma Square

ld.name: Hotel Grande Bretagne in Athens
ld.description: The Hotel Grande Bretagne is a bit of a departure for a Greek luxury hotel: rather than some sprawling compound out on a rock by the Aegean, this one is a Victorian mansion right in the bustling heart of Athens. Yes, you read that right — the meticulously restored facade is all Victorian, and wouldn't look out of place alongside some of London's classic hotels.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Monument in Athens
ld.description: This house is a late-19th-century work by Ernst Ziller, a man whose architectural fingerprints are all over modern Greece. After a substantial yet sensitive restoration by the local architecture firm MPlusM, it has become a small and chic boutique hotel that aims to preserve an important piece of local culture while updating it with contemporary design and luxury-hotel comforts.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: NOT Hotel in Athens
ld.description: In an artsy Athens neighborhood not far from the Temple of Hephaestus, there’s a centuries-old stone building with a colorful past: once a brothel, it later served as a barn, an army barracks, and later a film studio. Today it’s home to the character-filled NOT Hotel. The name is an acronym — NOT stands for No Ordinary Things — an apt description of the eclectic project, its carefully restored interiors enlivened by glamorous 1920s-inspired details. Set around a picturesque central courtyard planted with olive trees, flowers, and herbs are rooms and suites with exposed brick or stone walls, antique writing desks, patterned throw rugs, and marble bathrooms with walk-in showers. Other highlights include a stylish outdoor swimming pool and a culinary program centering around house-made olive oil and locally produced wines.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: One&Only Aesthesis in Athens
ld.description: Though the Athenian Riviera’s beach hotel scene had its heyday back in the 1960s, the region is undergoing a renaissance with the advent of stylish resorts like One&Only Aesthesis. This exclusive gated enclave, set on a peninsula overlooking Asteras Beach, features a vintage-inspired main building and a collection of luxurious bungalows. Some face the sea and others are tucked into Mediterranean gardens, but all have floor-to-ceiling windows and midcentury modern interiors lined with pale timber and native stone. Bungalows and waterfront villas open onto gorgeous private gardens with pools, fireplaces, and outdoor showers framed by olive trees.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: THE DOLLI at Acropolis, A Hotel to Live

ld.name: THE DOLLI at Acropolis, A Hotel to Live in Athens
ld.description: Plenty of Athenian hotels are set within sight of the Parthenon, but few do as much with the view as the Dolli at Acropolis. It’s set in a neoclassical building from 1925, to which has been added a rooftop infinity pool and an upscale international restaurant that takes in an extraordinary panorama. And what’s inside is far from shabby — this is not just a stylish boutique hotel but a luxurious one as well. The high ceilings and oversized windows make the rooms feel even larger than they are, and the décor is both visually distinctive and tastefully high-end.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Xenodocheio Milos in Athens
ld.description: Xenodocheio Milos is named not directly for the island of Milos but for chef Costas Spiliadis’s Milos restaurants, and you’d be right to suspect that this Athens city-center luxury hotel features a kitchen that’s substantially above average. The accommodations, too, are a cut above, walking the line between minimalism and warmth, with comforts that mark this as a proper high-end luxury boutique hotel. It’s got a small spa of its own, as well as facilities for Pilates and yoga; the restaurant, Estiatorio Milos, serves an artful interpretation of traditional Mediterranean flavors, and attracts locals and guests alike.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Acro Suites in Crete
ld.description: Perhaps inspired by similarly situated dwellings on the island of Santorini, Acro Suites brings cliffside romance and carved-rock drama to the north coast of Crete. This adults-only resort-style luxury boutique hotel is the smaller and more reserved sister to the Sea Side Resort, right next door — an arrangement that allows Acro Suites’ guests to use Sea Side’s substantial facilities, but not the other way around.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets 4 kg and under are allowed on property

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Domes Zeen Chania in Crete
ld.description: Domes Zeen Chania, on the northwest coast of Crete, is not only blessed with a spectacular natural setting — it’s also outfitted with top-flight luxury comforts, and thanks to its designers, the Berlin-based Lambs and Lions, it’s one of the most aesthetically distinguished hotels in the region, its modernist geometries warmed by natural textures and warm, earthy neutral tones.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Kapsaliana Village Hotel in Crete
ld.description: The historic village of Kapsaliana, built around an old olive mill and surrounded by Crete’s largest olive grove, was all but abandoned in the 1950s. Years later, a local architect discovered the place and transformed it into what it is today: an uncommonly restful and unusually memorable luxury resort by the name of Kapsaliana Village Hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Manili Boutique Suites & Villas in Crete
ld.description: Tucked away on an atmospheric side street in the Cretan village of Archanes, Manili Boutique Suites & Villas is perhaps a more modern and stylish luxury boutique hotel than you’d expect to find in this corner of the island, a little less than half an hour inland from the city of Heraklion.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Minos Palace Resort in Crete
ld.description: The spectacular Mirabello Bay on the northeastern coast of the island of Crete is the setting for Minos Palace Resort, an unapologetically high-end boutique-style resort whose peninsula location gives it sea views in just about every direction. The private-island illusion is only heightened by the fact that it’s an adults-only hotel; even though it’s just a mile outside of the seaside town of Agios Nikolaos, it achieves a laid-back tranquility that’s reminiscent of some much more secluded hotels.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Pnoé Breathing Life in Crete
ld.description: Pnoé means “breath” in Greek, and that’s exactly the idea when checking into Pnoé Breathing Life, a sleek beach resort on a private beach outside Crete’s largest city — inhale, exhale, and repeat, whether floating in your personal pool, relaxing in the state-of-the-art spa, or sipping cocktails at the rooftop bar.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Eliamos Villas Hotel & Spa in Kefalonia
ld.description: Eliamos Villas Hotel & Spa benefits, first and foremost, from a beautiful location on the south coast of Kefalonia, on a hillside above a beach, looking out over the Ionian Sea. Also auspicious: its owner is an interior designer, and judging by the look of the hotel’s 12 villas, a fine one indeed — these spaces combine crisp contemporary design and the warmth of materials that feel handmade, all without a hint of Greek-island kitsch. There’s a small spa as well as a gym with facilities for yoga and Pilates, and an outdoor infinity pool; the hotel’s restaurant and bar occupy an impressive open-air space.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: ALBERGO GELSOMINO in Kos
ld.description: Hotels in the Dodecanese don’t get much more historic than the century-old Albergo Gelsomino, designed and built in 1927 by Italian architect Rodolfo Petracco as a guesthouse for Italian officials. It stands right on the beach, a minute’s walk from the port and the old town, and its unique silhouette cuts a memorable figure along the seaside boulevard.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Lango Design Hotel & Spa in Kos
ld.description: Kos has been relatively late to embrace the boutique-hotel boom. With Lango Design Hotel & Spa, however, the island is making up for lost time. This 54-room adults-only luxury boutique hotel is as polished as they come, a vision in near-monochrome minimalism, set right across the road from Lambi Beach and a few minutes’ walk from the Kos town center.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: OKU Kos in Kos
ld.description: OKU Kos is an adults-only hideaway that takes the classic village idiom in a decidedly contemporary direction. The rooms and suites are divided among a number of crisply geometric villas, while in their interiors they’re warmed by earth tones, natural textiles, and a general boho-chic vibe. The best suites come with private pools, and the most extravagant units are the beachfront villas; at all levels, though, the accommodations are luxurious, if quietly so.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Amanzoe in Kranidi
ld.description: Aman has a hotel in Greece — while that’s not quite all we think you need to know, we’ll understand if a few of you are already entering your dates. Anyway, if you’re at all familiar with what the Aman group does, and you’ve ever laid eyes on a photograph of the Aegean coast, then you already know where we're going with this.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Kinsterna Hotel in Monemvasia
ld.description: Between the island paradise of the Cyclades and the chic boutiques of the capital, it’s no wonder the international traveler has scant attention left for some of Greece’s lesser-known destinations. One imagines, however, that fans of these lesser-known destinations like it that way. Every booking in Santorini is one more person with whom you won’t have to share Kinsterna, a thirteenth-century estate converted into a boutique hotel, a few miles down the Peloponnese coast from the medieval citadel of Monemvasia.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Amyth of Mykonos Agios Stefanos in Mykonos
ld.description: Just up the hill from the beach at Agios Stefanos is Amyth of Mykonos, a luxury boutique hotel with a decidedly warm, bohemian aesthetic alongside comforts that are normally the purview of a larger resort. Most of the suites come with either an outdoor hot tub or a private pool, and many also feature direct views out to sea. The hotel’s clean, modern lines are warmed by liberal use of natural materials; the textures of wood and stone reinforce the hotel’s connection with nature. Meanwhile the restaurant and poolside bar serve classic Mediterranean dishes and sophisticated cocktails.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Boheme Mykonos Town in Mykonos
ld.description: There are times when you don’t want to get away from it all. Mykonos isn’t exactly a desert island, but nobody’s asking it to be one. If you’re going there it’s because along with your sun and surf, to paraphrase the Bard, you want to see people and you want to see life. So why not skip the whole shipwreck fantasy and book in to a stylish boutique hotel in Mykonos town itself? We’ve got just the place, as you might well have guessed, and it goes by the name of Boheme Mykonos.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed upon request.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Cali Mykonos in Mykonos
ld.description: Arriving at Cali Mykonos is a slow reveal - an ancient olive tree, whitewashed walls, and then the Aegean stretching endlessly below. Carved into a cliff above Kalafatis Beach, it is a quieter, more refined take on Mykonos, where muted tones and contemporary Greek design set a soothing scene. A 130-meter infinity pool curves along the edge, a private beach awaits below, and days unfold between Pilates, yacht excursions, and freshly-caught seafood. A rare moment of stillness on an island known for its energy.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Deos Mykonos - A Myconian Collection Hotel

ld.name: Deos Mykonos - A Myconian Collection Hotel in Mykonos
ld.description: Mykonos pairs extraordinary beauty with some of Greece’s most impressive luxury hotels, many of which operate under the Myconian banner. Deos, named after the Greek word for “awe,” is one of them, and it’s aptly named — from its perch on a hillside above the old port it takes in a spectacular island panorama.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are permitted upon request; additional charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Ethereum Mykonos in Mykonos
ld.description: There’s no need to choose between elevated ocean views and easy beach access at Ethereum Mykonos. Set in the hills above the Aegean, this luxury boutique hotel offers sweeping vistas of the curving shoreline, but the beautiful Psarou beach — and one of the island’s most exclusive beach clubs — is just a short walk away. Suites are sophisticated and serene with exposed stone walls, floor-to-ceiling windows, modern decor in earth tones, and private terraces with plunge pools and sunbeds, with the best rooms dramatically positioned over the seascape below. Guests are welcome to use the stylish spa, fitness center, bars, and restaurants at the affiliated Palladium Hotel Mykonos across the street.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Kalesma Mykonos in Mykonos
ld.description: Mykonos is already as desirable as any destination in the Mediterranean, and the luxe and alarmingly stylish Kalesma only raises the stakes. It’s set on a hilltop on the island’s west side, fifteen minutes from town, and feels like a private refuge — one whose suites and villas pay tribute to classic Cycladic architecture as well as modern interior design, and feature Rick Owens furnishings among their adornments.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Myconian O in Mykonos
ld.description: They take sun-drenched Cycladic getaways seriously in the Myconian Collection. This family run local chain is committed to your relaxation, with O being the prime example. Relax under their parasols on the beach with a drink from the bar, then head back to your room with its moody-chic, black-and-white décor. Then, depending on what style of relaxation works for you, head to either the O’ Spa and its stunning cave pool, or ask the team to arrange adventures from horse riding to scuba diving.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Myconian Panoptis Escape in Mykonos
ld.description: Like its sister hotels, Myconian Panoptis Escape is a luxurious escape with dazzling sea views — in this case, 360-degree panoramas over Elia Beach and the bright blue Aegean from its clifftop perch. What further sets it apart is an air of exclusivity, thanks in part to the attentive butlers (or Artisans, as they’re called) that serve the hotel’s 21 stylish villas around the clock. Modern and boho-chic, the villas are outfitted with everything you could possibly need, and many have private pools or outdoor Jacuzzis facing the water. A large saltwater infinity pool and sanctuary-like spa offer additional space for relaxing like a Greek god or goddess.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed on request. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mykonos Blanc Hotel in Mykonos
ld.description: Think of a Mykonos luxury boutique hotel and it’s likely what you’re imagining bears a strong resemblance to the Mykonos Blanc Hotel. Set at one end of the picturesque south-facing Ornos Beach — a short walk from its sister hotel, the beachfront Mykonos Ammos Hotel — it’s a picture-perfect slice of Cycladic hospitality, a terraced village of whitewashed villas containing 42 minimalist-chic rooms and suites.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mykonos Bliss in Mykonos
ld.description: Some call it the “Island of the Winds,” but really, Mykonos is all about the water. With the Aegean Sea as a backdrop, you’d be hard pressed to find a vacation spot here that doesn’t make the most of its exposure to those iconic cerulean waters. But that’s what makes Mykonos Bliss so special: not only do you get incredible views and close proximity to one of the island’s most famous beaches, you also get your own private slice of aqueous paradise.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mykonos Grand Hotel & Resort in Mykonos
ld.description: You know what you’re getting into when you book a stay at a luxury hotel on a Greek island, and much of it comes in shades of white or blue. There’s the clear sky and the azure sea, the sparkling pool, the whitewashed stucco and diaphanous drapery billowing in the breeze. So what distinguishes Mykonos Grand Hotel & Resort from all the other gorgeous resorts on the so-called island of the winds?

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: NOMAD Mykonos in Mykonos
ld.description: Half a world away from the similarly named but unrelated boutique hotels in New York and Los Angeles, NOMAD Mykonos is a one-off, a small and luxurious 14-suite adults-only escape that promises splendid isolation on an island that’s not exactly a well-kept secret. The location helps: it’s on the southeast coast, halfway across the island from Mykonos town, a pleasant few minutes’ walk up the road from the lovely Kalo Livadi beach.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed upon request.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Numo Mykonos in Mykonos
ld.description: Small-scale, retro-chic, and environmentally friendly, Numo Mykonos is a refreshing antidote to the island’s more party-focused hotels. Housed in a beautifully restored historic building on a gently sloping hill above Kalafati Beach, it’s the work of a boutique hotel group that runs the popular Numo Ierapetra, on the island of Crete.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Palladium Hotel Mykonos in Mykonos
ld.description: Just up the hill from the lovely Psarou Beach and its glamorous beach club, a collection of modern whitewashed buildings houses the Palladium Hotel Mykonos. The architecture is Cycladic-inspired, but the rooms and suites are boho-chic, outfitted with wood, linen, raffia, and one-of-a-kind artisan-crafted details. All have spacious walk-in showers and furnished balconies, many facing the sea, and some feature private pools or open-air hot tubs. The main pool, surrounded by plush sunbeds, is lively by day and gorgeously illuminated at night. A pair of restaurants, a spa, and a fitness center mean you’ll barely have to leave the premises, though one of the island’s best beaches is just a short walk away.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Townhouse Mykonos in Mykonos
ld.description: It’s often the case that the hotels with the most unassuming names are also the most impressive ones. TownHouse Mykonos is no ordinary townhouse, but an 18th-century manor house in the island’s old town, a listed landmark restored, renovated, and expanded over the course of three years into the adults-only luxury boutique hotel you see today.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Cove Paros in Paros
ld.description: None of the Cyclades is an undiscovered secret, but Paros is quieter than some of its neighbors, and a hotel like Cove Paros does nothing to disturb that tranquility. It’s set just above the cove that gives it its name, and comprises some 45 luxurious, contemporary suites, each one provided with lavish bathrooms and plentiful outdoor lounge space — and the five signature suites come with private pools. The rest of the guests make do with the hotel’s impressive infinity pool, or find their way to the beach club for a sunset cocktail followed by dinner at RADA, the hotel’s impressive seaside restaurant.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Andronis Minois in Paros
ld.description: On the relatively sleepy west coast of the island of Paros, close to the capital but comfortably secluded above a picturesque little bay, is Andronis Minois, a 44-room boutique hotel in a style that’s equal parts modern minimalism and Cycladic tradition. It’s less a party hotel and more a luxurious little enclave, but that doesn’t mean it’s any less glamorous — its buildings combine a contemporary take on Greek architecture with a vibrant mix of Western Mediterranean influences, from the Italian Riviera to France, Spain, and even Morocco, all unified by the confident hand of its Athens-based designers.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets up to 10 Kilos are allowed

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Tainaron Blue Retreat in Peloponnese
ld.description: Legend has it that the entrance to the home of Hades, god of the underworld, could be found in a cave at Cape Tainaron, not far from Tainaron Blue Retreat. For a location associated with the underworld, this is a pretty idyllic spot: perfectly positioned at the southernmost point of the Greek mainland, undiscovered by the tourist crowds, boasting spectacular sea views to match any Aegean island (fittingly, it’s also said to have been home to a temple to Poseidon, god of the sea). Housed in a centuries-old tower that was designed to keep intruders out, the fully restored guesthouse now welcomes visitors from around the globe, but not too many of them — there are just three suites, one at the base of the tower, another in its upper section, and a third in the adjoining tower house.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Ammades All Suites Beach Hotel & Spa - Adults Only

ld.name: Ammades All Suites Beach Hotel & Spa - Adults Only in Rhodes
ld.description: No low-lying cluster of villas, Ammades All Suites Beach Hotel is a substantial seafront presence — but, as its name implies, it offers not a mega-resort experience but something far more private and small-scale. With just 45 suites, the hotel maintains a personal touch, while the atmosphere remains pleasantly tranquil—helped by its adults-only policy. And yet the comforts at Ammades go beyond typical boutique-hotel fare: Ammades Taste, the high-end restaurant, is joined by the more casual Ammades Seaside Restaurant and Bar.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets allowed: dogs up to 7 kg, max 1 per room. Extra charges apply; prior notification required.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Kókkini Porta Rossa in Rhodes
ld.description: A setting within the medieval city center of Rhodes would be remarkable enough; in Kókkini Porta Rossa a local family has transformed a derelict house, long ago associated with the Knights of Saint John, into a richly detailed and uniquely atmospheric six-room boutique hotel. It’s an amateur production in the best possible sense of the word: made not out of professional obligation but out of sheer love of the place. In its services it’s perhaps more bed and breakfast than hotel per se; the breakfast, however, is an extremely fine one, and your hosts have prepared a multitude of recommendations for getting around Rhodes.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Andronis Arcadia in Santorini
ld.description: Most hotels in Oia partake in the same southerly view of the volcanic caldera, but a few brave souls, Andronis Arcadia, opt for something different. Set on the back side of town, this stylish high-end resort faces to the northwest, looking out over the Aegean Sea and the islands in the distance. If it sounds like a sacrifice, it really isn’t — the sunsets, in particular, are extraordinary. But the most remarkable thing about it is the sense of seclusion you get from being just a few hundred meters off the beaten track.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Andronis Concept in Santorini
ld.description: The concept, essentially, is slow living, and indeed it’s hard not to linger for an extra moment over Andronis Concept’s elevated views of the Santorini caldera. It has much in common with other hotels of the genre, but manages to set itself apart with its generous spaces and an extra measure of refinement in its modernist-influenced, neutral-toned décor.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bellonias Villas in Santorini
ld.description: Somewhere on the long list of good things that originated in Greece — the Olympic Games, feta cheese, democracy — is architecture. There are the buildings you’ll view on sightseeing tours, the ancient temples and grand palaces of the Acropolis, and there’s the Cycladic tradition. These are the buildings you’ll actually sleep in and wander past while staying on the islands, the charming whitewashed houses and blue-domed churches you’ll never tire of photographing. Bellonias Villas, on Santorini, is a contemporary take on that quaintly rustic Cycladic aesthetic. Like the island’s older buildings, it’s all smooth stucco, clean lines, curving archways, and petite windows that reveal picture-perfect views of the Aegean Sea. But inside the hotel’s 27 villa suites, the look is modern and minimalist.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Canaves Epitome in Santorini
ld.description: Most every high-end hotel in Oia — maybe in all of Santorini — faces toward the volcanic caldera at the center of the island’s crescent arc. But Canaves Epitome means to set itself apart from the crowd, and it does so both literally and figuratively. Literally, with a position about a mile from the center of town, on the western extremity of the island’s north arm; this naturally leads to what sets it figuratively apart, which is its westward view of the island of Thirasia and the open sea beyond.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Canaves Sunday in Santorini
ld.description: Some destinations are about hard work and self-discovery, but Santorini is all about indulgence, luxury, and finding the optimal spot to catch a breathtaking Mediterreanean sunset. Often called the “supermodel” of the Greek islands, it’s known for the kind of stunning natural beauty that an average hotel would struggle to do justice to — luckily, the upscale Canaves Sunday is anything but an average hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets aren't allowed in the property.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Erosantorini in Santorini
ld.description: Erosantorini Luxury Private Estate & Suites is just what it says it is: a surprisingly substantial plot of land on an island where cozy cliffside perches are the rule, and a self-contained escape whose suites are often booked together as a single, sprawling four- or five-bedroom villa. The property cascades down the hillside, splitting the infinity pool into three distinct levels, and there’s a dramatic view of the caldera from just about every square foot of the estate. Meanwhile an open-air kitchen and dining area serve as a communal entertaining space, and each suite comes with either an outdoor Jacuzzi or a plunge pool.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Grace Hotel, Auberge Collection  in Santorini
ld.description: When it comes to architecture and interior design, there was only ever a hair’s breadth between the Cycladic tradition and the modern minimalist boutique hotel. Both revel in absence of ornament, in geometric lines and vast expanses of white. And in Grace Hotel Santorini the two idioms are brought seamlessly together. It’s near colorless, crisp-edged, clean-lined and packed with modernist furniture, and yet still it looks perfectly at home. And like any good Santorini hotel, Grace knows when to get out of the way and let you enjoy the view.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Istoria Hotel in Santorini
ld.description: Most Santorini hotels are forced to choose between an idyllic black sand beach or the famous elevated view of the volcanic caldera, but Istoria is the rare hotel that can offer both. The key is that it’s in two places at once: in Perivolos, 12 sea-facing suites make up Istoria Beach, while a few miles away in Firostefani, 9 more cave-house suites comprise the caldera-facing Istoria Cliff.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Katikies Garden Santorini in Santorini
ld.description: Located in Fira’s old Venetian neighborhood, Katikies Garden Santorini occupies a restored 18th-century monastery. High-arching whitewashed passageways open onto a charming central courtyard — home to the hotel’s stylish restaurant and wine bar — with palm trees, colorful bougainvillea, and an antique tiled fountain, while beautifully illuminated staircases lead to a rooftop pool overlooking the village, the sea, and the mountains beyond. Suites are elegant and modern with dark wood flooring and a color palette of white, silver, and deep emerald green; all have private patios, and many feature private plunge pools or open-air Jacuzzi tubs.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Katikies Santorini - Gea House in Santorini
ld.description: The differences between the best Santorini hotels are remarkably subtle; how to distinguish one sun-drenched, white-washed hotel on a scenic seaside cliff from the next? More than anything, it just comes down to execution — well, that and the sublimity of the views, but the photos say it all in that department. Katikies Gea House is hardly breaking new ground on Santorini — if anything, their vision of the quintessential Greek Island hideaway is even purer than the competition’s. It’s just that, at Kirini, all the fresh white paint is somehow more pristine, the infinity pool overlooking the sea that much more spectacular, the suites even sunnier and breezier, and the beds more perfectly cloud-like than the competition’s. Add to all that some of the best food on the island and a serene spa, and Gea House is a contender for the best hotel on an island with some serious competition.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Katikies Santorini - Pelagos House in Santorini
ld.description: On Santorini, the view’s the thing, and there may be none better than that from the pool deck at Katikies, looking out over the island’s submerged volcanic caldera and the sea beyond. This hotel is a feast for the eyes, not just a scenic overlook but a sparkling white modernist take on a traditional cliff dwelling, spilling down the steep hillside a hundred meters above the water.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Kivotos Santorini in Santorini
ld.description: Plenty of very fine Santorini hotels allow their impressive views of the caldera to do all the heavy lifting, elevating their whitewashed spaces into something that approaches the sublime. Kivotos Santorini, in contrast, isn’t afraid to engage the landscape and seascape directly: dark grey stone and shaded, cavern-like rooms directly refer to the black sand beaches as well as the volcanic forces that created this spectacle, and at the same time lend an extra measure of elegance to this extravagantly luxurious hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Limestone Santorini in Santorini
ld.description: Many of Santorini’s best hotels are located in traditional yposkafa, or cave houses built directly into the rocks of the caldera. Geography and historic preservation codes limit their size, which is particularly noticeable at Limestone Santorini, an intimate five-suite hotel in a beautifully restored cave house that dates back to 1925. The name refers to its traditional building materials, which include the island’s rich volcanic soil; great care has been taken both inside and out to harness the laid-back charm and rejuvenating powers of one of Greece’s most famous destinations.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Perivolas Lifestyle Houses in Santorini
ld.description: Sleeping in a cave sounds a bit like sleeping in a treehouse, or sleeping underwater; photogenic, to be sure, but questionable as a real-world lodging. But however unusual the concept might sound, Perivolas — encompassing a series of restored caves that once served as horse stables and fishermen’s homes, set into cliffs above the startlingly blue Aegean — looks and feels like a gorgeous boutique hotel on a Greek island. (There’s a certain logic to that, of course, because that’s exactly what it is.)

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Tsitouras Collection in Santorini
ld.description: Stunning sunset views, check. Whitewashed walls and complimentary cocktails, check. What distinguishes Tsitouras Collection from the various other high-end lodgings on Santorini is the hotel’s structure: unlike the sprawling resorts with infinity pools, Tsitouras is comprised of just five freestanding houses situated on a cliff overlooking the sea.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Villa Bordeaux in Santorini
ld.description: All of the boutique hotels around Santorini’s rim are variations on a theme, and it’s not hard to guess what this one’s angle is. Here the caldera views come with a French accent, and that’s enough to set Villa Bordeaux apart. It’s a rare splash of red in a sea of white, and is home to La Colline, the island’s only French fine dining restaurant. The suites, too, depart from the all-white Santorini custom, opting instead for warm and varied neutral tones and a dash of colorful art. Thanks to the hotel’s small capacity the poolside never feels busy; two of the four suites also feature private Jacuzzis with elevated views.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: ON Residence in Thessaloniki
ld.description: A glamorous 1920s waterfront mansion, originally occupied by a popular brewery, is now home to the elegant ON Residence. Many of this historical building’s finest features remain, from the carefully restored facade with decorative wrought-iron balconies and freshly painted yellow shutters to the interior’s curving marble staircases and high coffered ceilings.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Aristi Mountain Resort in Zagori
ld.description: There’s more to Greece than Athens, the islands and that long, squiggly coastline. In the country’s northwest, out along the border with Albania, is the rugged and mountainous region of Zagori. It’s a landscape of rocky cliffs, verdant slopes and tiny, ancient villages clinging to the hillsides. And among the many lost-in-time-looking villages, one of the most picturesque of all is Aristi — a smattering of traditional stone homes at the edge of a stunning national park, and home to Aristi Mountain Resort.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Contessina Suites & Spa in Zakynthos
ld.description: Right around the corner from the slightly larger Contessina Hotel, and a block from the west end of Tsilivi Beach, is the more intimate and more luxurious — and, crucially, adults-only — Contessina Suites & Spa. Its style is modern and rather minimal, with not a hint of island kitsch; in fact it’s sophisticated enough to feel quite urban, even while its compound-like design makes it feel like something of a world unto itself.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Leeda's Village in Zakynthos
ld.description: The typical Greek island experience involves a sun-bleached, arid cliffside somewhere in the Aegean. But Zakynthos, on the Ionian side of the Greek mainland, is not the typical Greek island. It’s only here that something as lush and green as Leeda’s Village could exist — a set of weathered but rather grand stone buildings nestled amidst olive groves, gardens, and lawns, offering an experience that’s subtle, even sedate, but no less sublime.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Lesante Cape in Zakynthos
ld.description: Despite a wave of tourism and a proliferation of all-night bars and clubs, the Greek island of Zakynthos is a place where tradition is revered. Nowhere is this more true than at Lesante Cape, an elegant resort that pays homage to Zakynthian culture, from architecture to cuisine. It’s a village within a village, namely the seaside hamlet of Akrotiri; the hotel has its own taverna, shops, church, café, and central square. And while the grand archways, whitewashed buildings, and scenic olive trees mirror elements of the world outside, there’s a luxurious spin and a modern sensibility to this particular interpretation of the island lifestyle.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Olea All Suite Hotel in Zakynthos
ld.description: A hillside escape on the Greek island of Zakynthos doesn’t have to invent a whole new hospitality concept, and Olea All Suite Hotel, indeed, is all about the execution. This tropical-modernist marvel avoids the easy clichés of island design, evoking maximum atmosphere from the textures of concrete and wood. Its suites are strung along a lagoon-like pool, creating almost a floating-villa effect; the Royal Spa is as dramatic as they come, and three restaurants and three bars serve locally sourced Mediterranean cuisine in a variety of environments, from the very casual poolside Cocoon to the double-height Omikron with its far-ranging views.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Porto Zante Villas & Spa in Zakynthos
ld.description: Even if you’ve got a reasonably complete working knowledge of the major Greek island destinations, you might not know Zakynthos. It’s the next one down from Kefalonia, on the Ionian side of the Peloponnese — and, more importantly, it’s a perfect little jewel of a place, featuring the ludicrously beautiful Navagio Beach among its dramatic landforms and seascapes. And, as you might have guessed, it’s the setting for an extraordinary hotel: Porto Zante Villas & Spa, a luxury resort just above a private beach, blessed with extraordinary sea views, elegant contemporary interiors, and all the high-end comforts you could reasonably wish for.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request but are not allowed in any areas which serve food or beverages.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay
